newsitem.title: UK: UK's SIB plans to broaden OEIC investment powers.
newsitem.headline: UK's SIB plans to broaden OEIC investment powers.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Investments Board (SIB) on Wednesday set out proposals for broadening the investment powers of open-ended investment companies (OEICs).

In a consultative paper outlining proposals for the next generation of OEICs, the SIB said the changes would bring the range of investments available to OEICs in line with those available to authorised unit trusts.
At present, only those OEICs which fall within the terms of the EU's UCITS Directive are permitted.

OEICs are closely modelled on UK unit trusts, but have some key differences. They will offer a single mid-market price rather than a bid-offer spread, and a corporate structure will allow them to borrow.
They were devised to pull more retail investors into the collective investment market, and allow British based fund managers to market a more familiar fund structure in Europe.
The next generation of OEICs would include money market instruments, fund of funds, futures and options, geared futures and options, and property.
Currently, OEICs can only invest in listed securities, other collective investment schemes and certificates of deposit.
OEICs have a corporate form, unlike unit trusts which fall under trust law and provide increased flexibility, including the ability to have different classes of shares.
A less prescriptive approach is balanced by enhanced disclosure to assist investors to make informed decisions, the SIB said.
An OEIC is a flexible pooled investment fund of variable size in corporate form and with a simple pricing structure. There is a high degree of protection for investors with emphasis on disclosure.
UCITS stands for Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities.
